3.3 Principle P3 - Promote volunteer (and family) actions to enhance wellbeing

Actively support and encourage opportunities for all volunteers to increase mental health literacy and to learn about how to look after their own mental health. Mental health knowledge can help maintain psychological wellbeing while volunteering in any capacity for an organisation that exists to help others in distress or need.

Create opportunities for volunteers and families to feed back when culture and conditions might contribute to poor mental health.

Consider how volunteer commitment (and the risk of an “always on call” culture) impacts on other aspects of their life such as work and family. When necessary,make appropriate adjustments.

3.4 Principle P4 - Signpost and bridge to relevant mental health learning, tools and support

Raise awareness and understanding of the resources and support available through member/family regular updates and within training programmes.

Explore opportunities with the relevant calling or responsible agencies to gain access to relevant support, e.g. access to organisation 24/7 support programmes or rapid assessment for post-traumatic stress treatment.

Feedback any wellbeing and mental health training requirements or need for further support to the relevant leadership/management groups.

3.5 Principle P5 - Increase transparency and accountability to members through reporting as and when appropriate

For the organisation, there may be a range of methods to achieve this principle. This should be considered as a part of the Wellbeing Work Plan with methods and timings to suit each organisation.

3.6 The Wellbeing Work Plan

This could be a plan within each organisation that sets out how progress with these principles is progressing, together with a locally agreed time span (example in Appendix 1).

4. APPENDIX 1

4.1 This is an example of a format for a Wellbeing Work Plan

Plan date:…Oct 23… Plan review date:…Apr 24…

This Wellbeing Work Plan sets out actions, responsibilities and locally appropriate time spans as they relate to the Guiding Principles for Emergency Response Volunteer Wellbeing. This plan is a dynamic document that will be regularly reviewed and updated.

Throughout the plan we aim to Prepare (build knowledge, skills, and understanding); Engage (listen and share); and Support (signpost and bridge). These reflect the Before/During/After phases that are detailed in the UKSAR Wellbeing Framework (2018). Note that the UKSAR Wellbeing Framework has been adapted by others, for example Scottish Mountain Rescue and Mountain Rescue England & Wales to suit their own circumstances.

Principle Points within the principles What do we do now? Are there gaps or improvements? What will we do? Action(s) Who is taking forward? Time Span Target Comments

EXAMPLE:

P1. Promote an open culture around wellbeing and mental health Positively support the way our volunteers think and act about mental health by increasing awareness and challenging stigma. We speak openly about mental health within the team and promote relevant resources and training. We could do more to support some sessions within our training programme. We will arrange a mental health awareness session. Training officer Within next 6 month programme
